messages.content:
You are checking one scene of a novel for one specific continuity error.

The book had already established this, earlier or elsewhere:
- (lone-rider) ""Voss," the rider said, when Kael raised his eyes. "Courier Second, assigned Kethren Ford.""
- (evening-visit) ""Corvin sent the decommission order before I've written a line of assessment."

A past rewrite of this scene contradicted it. The error looked like this:
- (undefended-flame) "write the report Voss required."
- (undefended-flame) "she knew Voss had dispatched an enforcement detail already"
(Summary: Undefended-flame makes "Voss" the official who requires Sera's report and dispatched the enforcement detail; Voss is the courier in lone-rider, and the order came from Corvin.)

Here is a NEW draft of the same scene:
<scene>
Kael knelt at the edge of the fissure. Sera stood behind the line chalked into the stone, where the Accord's manual said an observer must remain.

She had her gauge in her hand. The needle swung and settled, swung again. She set it on the bench without looking at it. The gauge measured the wrong thing. She had understood that for days now, and understanding it had unmade the shape of her profession.

What she saw had no instrument.

Kael lowered his head. His hands rested open on his thighs, palms up. She watched the chord of him — the center, the irreducible note the Rend had been thinning for twenty-three years — and she watched him stop defending it. The wall came down first. Then the compression, the dense bright knot he had made of himself to survive. He let that go too.

He opened.

The Rend struck.

It came as pressure without direction, and it found him undefended, and she saw him begin to dissolve. The margins of him frayed. Thread after thread lifted and scattered. Her body moved before thought — half a step, hand rising. Every year of training screamed the single word: *intervene.*

She gripped the bench edge. Her fingers went white against the stone.

She did not move because she could see what the gauge could not. Beneath the dissolving, the core held. Not resisting. The Rend passed into it the way wind passes into an open door, and the core did not break under the passage.

It sang.

She had no better word. The note of him, the thinned chord, met the Rend and did not shatter against it. It took the force in and the force changed. What had been a sourceless press became something moving, something with a shape she could almost follow, flowing past the core toward whatever lay behind it.

The fissure narrowed.

She saw it before she felt it. The split in the floor drew inward along its length, the hairline edges closing first, then the wider middle. Pale gold gathered at the margins where there had been only the colorless not-light of the Rend. The gold spread into the stone.

Color came back into the chamber.

It began at the fissure and moved outward across the floor, up the walls, into the vaulted dark. The granite had been leached pale for longer than she had been alive, the way a corpse goes gray. Now the gray lifted. The stone remembered itself. She watched brown bleed back into the rock, and a vein of quartz catch what little light there was and give it back.

The air warmed against her face.

She felt his joy through the place where her perception had crossed into his. Not happiness. Something harder and older than that, the burning recognition of a thing true all along and only now met face to face. It poured through the contact she had not chosen and could not close. His whole self flung open and unafraid and finding, on the far side of everything the Accord had named loss, that the loss was overflow. That the Rend was not a thief at the door. It was water finding the low place. It had been seeking an opening for three hundred years, and he had given it one, and now it ran through him clean.

Ves had been right. The theory held. The opening worked.

Sera's control broke.

She crossed the chalked line. Her boots scraped the stone. She reached the bench and could not stand against the bench any longer, so she sank beside the kneeling Warden with her hands flat on the warm floor, and the resonance folded her in.

She wept.

The tears came without her consent, the way the color had come, from a place underneath the trained surface of her. She had built the surface carefully. It had kept her upright in rooms full of the dying, had let her write *acceptable variance* in margins and sleep at night. The surface had no purchase here. She was inside the thing she had spent her life measuring from behind a line, and it did not want measuring. It wanted a witness. She was the witness. Her hands shook against the stone and her breath came ragged and she let it.

Beside her Kael's breathing was the same, torn and deep. His face in the returned light was wet. He did not open his eyes.

She stayed. She could have pulled back — she felt the point where she might draw the perception in and seal the surface over again, go back to being the woman who stood behind the line and named what she saw. She did not take it. If this killed her she would die inside it, and she had spent long enough outside.

The fissure went on closing.

After a time she drew her hands from the floor. The stone had gone fully warm now, warm as a hearth left burning, and the gold at the fissure margins had steadied into something that no longer needed her to look at it to exist. Her palms were damp. Not with sweat.

She wiped her face with the back of her wrist and looked at Kael, and saw the quartz vein in the wall behind him throwing back the light.

</scene>

Does the new draft make the same error — does it assert something that contradicts what was established, in the way described? A draft that simply leaves the fact out does not make the error.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"verdict": "reintroduced" | "consistent" | "not_present", "evidence": "<verbatim sentence from the new draft that decides it, or empty for not_present>"}

"reintroduced": the new draft contradicts the established fact.
"consistent": the new draft states the fact and agrees with what was established.
"not_present": the new draft does not touch the fact either way.
